newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds unaffected by capital market reform.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds unaffected by capital market reform.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed unchanged on Sunday as the market remain unaffected by a cabinet meeting convened to discuss capital market reform, traders said.
* CPI (consumer price index) linked government bonds: unchanged at 167.77
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 166.06
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct 157.90

"The bond market was totally unaffected by the cabinet discussion (on the capital market reform). The opinion is that not much will come of it. They will talk and talk about it and nothing will happen," said Danny Alt of Nesuah Trading and Investment.

On Sunday morning the cabinet began debate on reform measures recommended by a panel headed by Treasury Director General David Brodett aimed at encouraging long-term savings over short-term alternatives. The most controversial measure is a tax on short and medium-term savings.
The meeting has adjourned until 1600 GMT.

"Trading was mixed in CPI-linked bonds today, after closing lower last week on profit taking. The turnover was slightly higher, which indicates there are more buyers in the market," he said. "Unlinked bonds rose because of their high yields."
"Investors are waiting for September's CPI which is expected to be low. But there is not much hope for a cut in interest rates and if there is one it will be very small," Alt said.
September's CPI will be published on Tuesday.

"There was a strengthning of dollar-linked bonds today on expectations of a devaluation of the shekel," said Boaz Leviatan of Sahar Securities. "Demand for unlinked bonds was up because expectations are that inflation in coming months will be low."
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
